selections.comment: A fascinating novice to kick off the card can go to the once-raced ERNST BLOFELD. The Frankel colt maded a promising debut when third over 8f at the track earlier this month, keeping on nicely. The yard's newcomers often improve from debut and this this step up in trip looks ideal as his full-brother won the Qatar Derby (Listed) over 10f. Of the newcomers, Modern Style has to be on the shortlist from the Charlie Appleby yard. An expensive purchase, he's bred to suit 10f and the yard are no strangers to sending out first-time winners. Sword Of Wessex should suit the step up in trip after his second at Sandown last season. And while he needs to improve on that, fancy entries in the Dante and Derby suggest connections have seen more than he's shown on the track. Of the other newcomers, Criminal and Spanish Train both tick plenty of boxes on pedigree.

selections.comment: With caveats around all the leading contenders, it could pay to back OKEECHOBEE, the highest-rated runner in the race. Although off the track since his Gordon Richards Stakes (G3) win at Sandown last April (Checkandchallenge behind), this lightly raced gelding goes well fresh and was second in this race last season off a long absence. Military Order demands respect. The Godolphin runner had excuses for his heavy-ground Longchamp blowout when last seen, but won the Winter Derby on Tapeta prior to that and has run well fresh previously. Lion's Pride should be doing his best work late. Behind the selection in this race last season, stamina looks his forte and the 5yo may just be sharper now following a gelding operation. Botanical looks the pick of those runners with a race under their belts, while Teumessias Fox, 3/4 at the track, could outrun his price.

Although well held in the Snowdrop Fillies' Stakes here last time, the drop back in class will suit as the filly has solid form in this grade.

selections.comment: Plenty in with chances in this trappy staying handicap. LEGACY POWER, well below form off a long absence when a beaten favourite here last time, could bounce back to form if forgiving that last run as he's a leading contender for this top course jockey/trainer combination on last season's C&D form. Believitanducan was ideally suited by the step up in trip when scoring at Beverley in July last season. The gelding, who returns to the Flat after two wins from three runs over hurdles subsequently, is in the mix on Polytrack debut. Cinnodin can make his presence felt off top weight. The gelding has a good strike-rate on the all-weather, was a winner off 72 here last time out and a 3lb rise may not stop him over a C&D that suits. Alex The Great races off a career-high mark here but is a previous C&D winner and makes the shortlist.

With a strong pace all but guaranteed in this line up Coastguard Station could stay on up the hill into a place on favoruable good ground.

Excello is another arriving seeking a hat trick and looks fairly treated returning to handicaps given a horse he beat at Exeter last time went close in a hot Aintree handicap after. Top weight Mr Escobar from the Mullins yard isn't yet fully exposed over hurdles and is fairly treated on the best of his Irish form. He didn't beat much in a Sedgefield maiden last time but never came off the bridle and he may prove better than tihs opening mark. Elysian Knight beat Authentic Legacy decisively here last time and should confirm that form on these revised terms.

selections.comment: He's A Latchico was a ready winner last time back on better ground and with plenty of mileage in his mark on his flat form is likely to prove popular for a local yard with a good record here. However, it was hard not to be impressed with the slick jumping of PUBLIC ENEMY in his ready C&D maiden win. He beat a useful flat performer that day and an opening mark of 107 may well underestimate him. He will likely need to be ridden more conservatively due to the early pace in the race but his debut effort suggests that won't be an issue. One of those setting the pace is likely to be Little Soiree who stopped quickly last time but had been showing a consistent level of form previously. She is likely to bounce back quickly on this faster ground and could hold on for a place.

selections.comment: BOASTY is taken to land a weak event. Ivan Furtado's charge continues to slip down the weights and is now 9lb better in than his last winning mark, achieved here over 2f furlongs shorter. There have been much more encouraging signs of late that he is finding his level again and a further pound drop for his most recent run (when 2nd here over 1m2f) could be enough for him to get back to wining ways over a trip he's not often tried before but performed up to his general level in two of his three attempts.  Moon Over The Sea would probably have been the selection but for a disappointing run here on Saturday over 1m6f as he had been firing prior to that with three seconds and a win (over 1m6f here) in recent months. The son of Sea The Moon should find the drop back to 1m4f a slight positive if anything but will need to up his game a tad. Two Plus Two is feared if in the same mood as his last couple of runs, both here, the fomrer over CD but tends to find a few too good. Navendon, seen more regularly over the jumps has a fair shot back on the Flat and shouldn't be discarded lightly

selections.comment: BALLARAT BERTIE can bounce back to top form and record a second course and distance win after a blip latest when dropped back to a mile at Southwell. This track suits much better, his two best career efforts have come here, and the step back up two furlongs is ideal. There's scope for a bit more and he should go close. Sweet Cicely looks the main danger having looked very close to finding her level last time (beaten under 2l) and dropped a further pound looks primed for a big run over a trip that looks as if it should suit (fair 5th of 9 only try and this tigh track should suit better than the galloping nature of Newcastle). Synergism is interesting but with the huge step up in trip is a bit too risky and Electric Bass could be a bigger danger on handicap bow over trip that's likely to suit better than the mile plied so far

selections.comment: ELLAND ROAD GIRL arrives in top order having opened her account on sixth attempt last time. It's possible the switch to turf was responsible for much of the improvement shown but her win stands out in a tight affair and she did run well over CD last month. Psychodrama is another to have opened their account last time out. That win came at Kempton on Polytrack but she's gone well here and holds every chance again. Gogo Yubari went close prior to a poor effort last time and as a course and distance winner has to be taken seriously. She could bounce back now eased back in grade but Rogue Dancer is feared more. Jack Jones's filly has improved with each run and landed a nursery handicap at Southwell in October when last seen. If fit to do justice off a layoff a bold show can be expected

selections.comment: Midnightattheoasis has improved rapidly this year and has to be taken seriously again seeking an incredible six-timer. He's been difficult to get a proper handle on as he's been winning with little to spare the last four of his wins. He could repeat the trick again here but on balance a futher 7lb rise looks likely to anchor him. He's taken on with REIGNING PROFIT. Maxine Carr's gelding knocked loudly on the door last time when going down by the narrowest of margins having been eased to this grade. From a pound lower than his last winning mark he can go one better here over course and distance he's won at. The consistent Recon Mission will be popular in his double attempt but a 7lb rise will be tough to defy and Buraback looks a likelier danger having hit form again. The slight rise in grade tempers enthsusiasm for Deerk Shaw's gelding
